anchors.note: When the compiled script runs, the inclusive range opcode creates the `Range` object with the negative integer begin and negative float end produced by the parser.
The compiled splat expression from step 6 is executed, so mruby must convert the just-created range object into an array through `mrb_ary_splat`.
Because the splatted object is a `Range`, `mrb_ary_splat` dispatches `to_a`, and `Range#to_a` immediately delegates numeric ranges to the vulnerable C helper `__num_to_a`.

Inside the integer-begin/float-end branch, the begin endpoint is lossy-cast from `mrb_int` to `mrb_float`. For the PoC's large magnitude on this 64-bit/double build, that conversion collapses the integer begin to an imprecise floating value that will also be used as the loop variable.
The end endpoint is loaded as `mrb_float` as well, so both range bounds are now compared and sized in floating-point rather than in exact integer arithmetic.

The destination extent is derived from the rounded float difference `(mrb_int)(b - a) + 1`, then `ptr = RARRAY_PTR(ary)` exposes that storage. For the witness, this reserves only a small array even though the subsequent loop will not make matching progress.

Because the range is inclusive, the code enters the `while (a <= b)` loop instead of the exclusive branch. With the PoC's rounded large endpoints, `a <= b` holds and later `a += 1.0` may fail to move `a` to a new representable float, so the loop's write count is no longer bounded by the capacity computed in step 12.

Sink. The loop issues another 8-byte store through `ptr[i++]` after the small array reserved in step 12 has been exhausted. The saved crash trace reports `WRITE of size 8` and identifies this exact line, `src/range.c:403:22`, as the heap-buffer-overflow site.
